cl: Drift detection answers whether a spec still points at code that exists
bc: a spec whose symbols have vanished is worse than no spec, because agents trust it

cl: The Stop hook blocks only on drift that is new since the previous run
bc: blocking on the full drift set re-fires the same block every turn while the drift persists, which traps the agent in a loop it cannot exit

cl: Stateless drift reporting in the Stop hook
bc: observed in a real session: the agent was caught in a loop because every Stop re-emitted the identical block reason

cl: The drift cache in .specgraph/last-drift-report.json must be written on every hook run, including when drift is empty
bc: a stale cache would suppress a genuinely new drift report on the following run

cl: implements entries with type 'file' are resolved against File nodes, all other types against CodeSymbol nodes
bc: checking file entries against CodeSymbol always failed, so every type:file link was reported as broken

cl: Specs with status 'archived' are excluded from drift detection
bc: archived specs describe retired behaviour, so their dead symbol links are expected rather than a defect

cl: tsup strips backslash escapes from template literals, so an escaped backtick in a skill string becomes a bare backtick and breaks the compiled output
bc: the emitted JS then parses the skill text as a template literal and throws ReferenceError at runtime

cl: Skill text must not contain backticks inside template literals; use double quotes instead
PHP method symbol ids have the form filePath::ClassName.methodName, never filePath::methodName
bc: a spec written with the short form silently fails to resolve and surfaces as drift rather than as a spec error

cl: namespace_definition counts as a container node in the PHP parser
bc: braced namespace syntax nests declarations one level deeper, so without it classes in braced namespaces were skipped

cl: Spec context is injected via a PreToolUse hook using hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext
bc: PostToolUse runs async and cannot inject context, and the Stop hook only supports decision/reason, so PreToolUse is the only point where an agent can be told what a file is specified to do before editing it

cl: The context hook exits successfully and silently when no specs match the edited file
bc: a non-zero exit or noisy output on every unspecced edit would train agents to ignore the hook

cl: The CLI calls process.exit(0) after the command completes instead of returning normally
bc: V8 runs GC finalizers for tree-sitter and LadybugDB native addons in an unspecified order at shutdown, which segfaults on macOS

cl: tsup does not typecheck — only 'tsc --noEmit' catches type errors
bc: esbuild strips types without checking them, so a green build says nothing about type correctness

cl: Knowledge is stored as NDJSON, one record per line, with git merge=union
bc: records are immutable and carry unique ids, so a textual conflict is always resolvable by taking both sides — which merge=union does automatically, but only if each record occupies exactly one line

cl: YAML as the knowledge record format
bc: YAML coerces unquoted dates to Date objects, which already forced a 'string | Date' union in the spec frontmatter type, and multi-line records are incompatible with merge=union

cl: Markdown with frontmatter as the knowledge format
bc: its only advantage is prose rendering for humans, and the markdown body was already dead weight — agents wrote almost everything into frontmatter because the body was stored as an unqueryable blob

cl: Record keys are abbreviated to two characters on the wire
bc: the schema is explained once per session in the skill (O(1)) while keys are paid per injected record (O(n)), so short keys win from roughly twenty records upward

cl: Record timestamps are always UTC in YYYYMMDDHHIISS form
bc: the format carries no timezone, so agents running in different zones would produce an unorderable history

cl: Records are immutable; a correction is a new record carrying ss (supersedes)
bc: immutability is what makes merge=union safe — on mutable records it would silently resolve to a wrong merge

cl: ABOUT edges are only created against nodes that already exist; unresolved subjects are reported, never stubbed
bc: materialising a stub node for a missing symbol would make drift undetectable, because every subject would then always resolve

cl: Record columns are named when_ and then_, not when and then
bc: when and then collide with Cypher keywords

cl: ensureSchema creates each missing table individually rather than all-or-nothing
bc: the previous version returned early if the Spec table existed, so a database built by an older release could never gain a newly added table without a full rebuild

cl: given/when/then are valid only on kind 'behavior' and are required there
bc: this makes kind selection mechanical — writing a scenario forces kind 'behavior' — replacing the judgement call that previously caused business_rule and software_requirement to be used interchangeably

cl: A record with several subjects in the same file returns once per matching ABOUT edge
bc: Cypher yields one row per edge, so any query feeding hook injection must use DISTINCT or the agent sees duplicated context

cl: Drift detection answers whether a knowledge record still points at code that exists
bc: a record whose subject has vanished is worse than no record, because agents trust it

cl: The drift cache in .specgraph/last-drift-report.json must be written on every hook run, including when drift is empty
bc: a stale cache would suppress a genuinely new drift report on the following run

cl: The markdown spec path was removed entirely; knowledge lives only in records
bc: the spec body was stored as an unqueryable blob and agents wrote almost nothing into it, so the whole path was 1550 lines carrying frontmatter that records model better

cl: Per-status filtering of records during drift detection, mirroring the old archived-spec skip
bc: records have no status field — supersede replaces it, and a superseded record is already excluded from drift by the live filter

cl: The analyze state cache outlives graph.db, so deleting only the database makes plain analyze silently under-index
bc: the cache claims every file is already indexed, so nothing is re-scanned; analyze now forces a full rebuild whenever the graph holds no symbols

cl: Only live records can drift; superseded records must never be reported as unresolved
bc: a record superseded because its code was renamed points at the old symbol by definition, so reporting it would make every rename add permanent noise

cl: writeSkills must prune specgraph-owned skill dirs no longer in SKILLS, or renamed/removed skills orphan on disk after upgrade
bc: it only ever wrote the current set; an ownership marker in each generated SKILL.md lets it delete its own stale dirs without touching hand-written user skills

cl: Every indexRecords call site must pass projectDir, or file-path subjects for unwalked files (docs, ADRs, manifests) never resolve
bc: the file-exists fallback that creates a File node is gated on projectDir; records index omitted it, so ADR subjects reported as drift despite the file being present

cl: bootstrap is split: the CLI is a directable deterministic scanner, an agent skill carries the judgment about where knowledge lives
bc: where decisions and docs live varies per project, so hardcoding ADR locations in a scanner was wrong; the deterministic sources with no location ambiguity (markers, reverts) stay zero-config, everything needing judgment moves to the knowledge-bootstrap skill

cl: deepMerge concatenated hook arrays unconditionally, so every init/upgrade run stacked another copy of the specgraph hooks
bc: the merge must dedup structurally-identical entries to stay idempotent; it now self-heals files that already accumulated duplicates while preserving distinct user hooks

cl: File watching uses @parcel/watcher, not Node fs.watch
bc: the native backend delivers absolute paths and reliable cross-platform events, removing the macOS subdirectory-enumeration workaround that fs.watch required

cl: Do not watch the project root on macOS; enumerate include subdirs as watch roots so .specgraph is never watched
bc: macOS FSEvents can coalesce events to the watch-root level with an empty relative path that bypasses shouldIgnore; keeping .specgraph out of watchRoots makes the ignore structural

cl: Agent hooks live in IDE settings files, not .git/hooks
bc: git hooks are excluded from VCS and fire outside AI sessions so their output never reaches the LLM; settings hooks fire during AI sessions and feed back directly to the model

cl: Project config lives in .specgraphrc.json at the repo root, not under .specgraph/
bc: .specgraph/ is gitignored for the binary graph DB and incremental state; configuration belongs in VCS alongside the knowledge source of truth

cl: Replace tree-sitter native addons with pure-TypeScript regex parsers
bc: reverted in 3a9c043; tree-sitter remains the parser backend

cl: engines is restricted to Node 20 and 22
bc: tree-sitter has no Node 24 prebuilt binary yet

cl: Cursor file-scoped knowledge is delivered via specgraph rules writing .cursor/rules/*.mdc with globs
bc: Cursor preToolUse cannot inject additionalContext; a rule with globs and alwaysApply false is the only documented mechanism to auto-attach knowledge when a matching file is in context

cl: writeRules prunes only .mdc files that contain RULE_MARKER; hand-written Cursor rules must not carry that marker
bc: without the marker check, regenerating rules would delete user-authored .cursor/rules the scanner did not create

cl: Cursor reads .cursor/hooks.json (version 1, camelCase events), not .cursor/settings.json
bc: Cursor shares no hook field names with Claude Code; copying the Claude schema into settings.json leaves Cursor with a file it never reads

cl: Deliver pre-edit knowledge in Cursor via specgraph context on a PreToolUse hook
bc: Cursor preToolUse accepts only permission, messages, and updated_input — not hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext — so the Claude context hook pattern does not work here

cl: Cursor hooks run specgraph rules on sessionStart and after Write so .mdc files stay in sync with the graph
bc: rules are derived output with no pre-edit refresh hook; stale rules would omit new records until the agent manually re-ran specgraph rules

cl: OpenCode experimental config shell hooks run analyze and plain check only — drift feedback goes through the specgraph-drift plugin on session.idle
bc: OpenCode config hooks are fire-and-forget shell commands that do not read stdout JSON; Claude-style check --hook-output output is ignored there

cl: OpenCode has no pre-edit knowledge injection — agents must call get_records_for_symbol via MCP before editing
bc: OpenCode has no rules generator and no PreToolUse context hook equivalent; only file_edited analyze keeps the graph in sync

cl: Record drift in OpenCode is surfaced by a plugin that runs check --hook-output --format opencode and calls client.session.prompt with the prompt field
bc: That is the only path that feeds drift text back into an OpenCode session; config hooks cannot consume hook JSON

cl: init/upgrade install post-checkout and post-merge hooks that rebuild the graph, plus a pre-commit hook running check --staged
bc: a branch checkout swaps the tree under the graph, so the next drift check reports the old branch's symbols as missing — a false positive that trips the Stop hook; rebuilding on checkout/merge removes it

cl: Every specgraph skill name must start with 'knowledge-'
bc: the .gitignore ignores generated skills by the knowledge-* glob so hand-written skills stay committable; a skill without the prefix would get committed and fork the source of truth

cl: Open Knowledge Format (OKF), the external standard this source/ref design aligns with
source is its own record kind carrying rf (the document); rf is valid only on source and required there
bc: a source pointer is 'go read this', semantically distinct from claims to obey; mirroring the given/when/then-only-on-behavior rule keeps kind selection mechanical and avoids fuzzing a constraint with an attached link

cl: A source record with sb (code subjects) rides the existing PreToolUse injection — editing that code surfaces 'consult Y'
bc: this is the bridge from code-independent domain knowledge to code: no new hook machinery, the same ABOUT-edge query picks it up, and without sb it is pure domain knowledge found by search

cl: The MCP server runs ensureSchema once on startup and wraps every tool dispatch in diagnoseError
bc: handlers open read-only, so a DB predating a column migration failed every query with a raw -32603 binder error and no recovery path; migrate-on-start prevents it and the wrapper turns any residual DB error into an actionable rebuild command

cl: analyze rebuilds records in the same pass as symbols when knowledge.ndjson has records
bc: analyze and records index were separate, so a rebuilt graph had symbols but zero records and every record query returned a silent [] — one command now keeps both current and the git hooks that run analyze keep records fresh too

cl: The README MCP tool list must match the server's dispatched tools; tests/readme.test.ts enforces it
bc: it drifted to advertise the whole deleted spec surface, so agents planned against tools that 404

cl: analyze must reindex records even on a symbol skip, since knowledge.ndjson changes independently of source
bc: gating record indexing on mode!==skip left a record added without a code change unindexed, and its subject was reported as drift

cl: In the MCP dispatch, delegated tool branches must be 'return await handleX(...)', not 'return handleX(...)'
bc: an unawaited returned promise's rejection escapes the surrounding try/catch in an async function, so a failing delegated handler reached the agent as a raw -32603 while inline await'd branches were diagnosed

cl: Every CLI command handler owns its DB lifecycle: open, try/finally close — never leak a connection
bc: handlers run as one-shot processes; a leaked connection can wedge the native LadybugDB addon at exit

cl: A directory subject is stored as a File node with kind='dir' and applies recursively to its whole subtree via segment-boundary ancestor matching
bc: reusing the File node avoids any schema migration (ABOUT and the drift known-set already cover File), and segment matching (not raw string prefix) stops foo/bar leaking into foo/barbaz

cl: Directory ancestor matching must split on / segments, never use raw startsWith
bc: string prefix would make a record at foo/bar wrongly apply to foo/barbaz/x.php — different directories that share a textual prefix

cl: A d:/t:/n: provenance pointer is verified to exist at write time (records add / add_record reject an absent file) and re-checked continuously as fabricatedRefs by check, CI, and the Stop hook
bc: specgraph exists to skip manual review, so a fabricated source must fail structurally rather than wait in a review queue; filesystem existence is unambiguous, which makes a hard write-time gate safe with zero false positives

cl: A draft/verified trust-state (a status field on records, promoting draft to live only after gates pass)
bc: it reintroduces the manual-review step specgraph exists to remove; the agent must manage the ndjson autonomously, so verification is mechanical and immediate, not a promotion queue

cl: The CLI entry must exit with process.exitCode, not a hard-coded process.exit(0)
bc: forcing 0 swallowed the non-zero exits that check (invalid/fabricated records) and a rejected records add set, so CI and pre-commit silently passed on fabricated provenance

cl: Record drift in OpenCode is surfaced by a plugin that runs check --hook-output --format opencode and calls client.session.prompt with the prompt field
bc: That is the only path that feeds drift text back into an OpenCode session; config hooks cannot consume hook JSON

cl: The product and CLI are named shanpan (was specgraph); on-disk layout is .shanpan/ and .shanpanrc.json, with migrateLegacyLayout renaming a pre-existing .specgraph/ layout in place on startup
bc: renaming rather than rebuilding preserves committed knowledge.ndjson byte-for-byte, so a repo bootstrapped under the old name does not silently read as empty — the 'your data is in the old place' failure the tool exists to avoid

cl: Knowledge skills keep the knowledge-* prefix (knowledge-lookup/record/check/bootstrap), not a shanpan-* product prefix, even after the specgraph→shanpan rename
bc: the skill name is a trigger surface that should describe the task so an agent picks the right one; 'shanpan-record' names the tool, not the job. Committability/ownership is already handled by the knowledge-* .gitignore glob plus the shanpan-managed-skill marker, so the visible name need not carry the brand

cl: Generated Cursor rules stay flat in .cursor/rules/ with a shanpan- filename prefix; they are NOT moved into a .cursor/rules/shanpan/ subdirectory
bc: our rules rely on Cursor's glob auto-attach (globs + alwaysApply false), which is reported to fire unreliably from subfolders; a subdirectory buys only cosmetic tidiness while risking the one behavior that matters. The shanpan- prefix plus RULE_MARKER prune already isolate ownership without a subfolder

cl: Whether Cursor applies .mdc rules from subdirectories of .cursor/rules, and how reliable glob auto-attach is from a subfolder
The Python parser extracts constants only for SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE names (module and class level); lowercase module-level assignments are skipped
bc: every Python module assigns lowercase locals/config at top level; extracting them all as 'constant' symbols would flood the graph with noise nothing anchors knowledge to. ALL_CAPS is the language's own constant convention

cl: In the Python parser, a call to a Capitalised bare name is recorded as call_kind 'instantiation' and a lowercase one as 'static_call' — a PascalCase convention heuristic, not type inference, because Python has no 'new' keyword to distinguish construction from a function call

Symbols must be deduped by id before insertSymbols — CodeSymbol.id is a PRIMARY KEY, and real code produces several symbols sharing one file::fqn id (Python @overload, TypeScript overload signatures and declaration merging, redefinitions under if TYPE_CHECKING). Without dedupeById the batched CREATE aborts with a duplicate-key violation
bc: found on the real rich codebase: rich/containers.py::Lines.__getitem__ is @overloaded and crashed analyze until dedupeById (last-wins, keeps the implementation) was added on both the full and incremental paths

cl: The knowledge-record anchoring guidance requires the subject to be what the claim is ABOUT, not merely near it: anchor where you'd want the warning mid-edit; repeated sibling leaves (three composer.json) mean the claim belongs to their shared parent; workflow/tooling knowledge anchors at the directory whose work it governs, not a scatter of config files
bc: agents obeyed 'most specific anchor that is true' by pinning a test-runner gotcha to three composer.json files it was not about, so it would never surface when running tests. 'Most specific' needed an aboutness counterweight

cl: Skill examples must stay language-neutral: span the supported languages (TypeScript, Python, PHP) with none dominating, and never hard-code a real dogfood project's paths (apps/bmf) or one ecosystem's tooling as the sole illustration
bc: dogfooding on a PHP/Symfony monorepo leaked composer.json, Infrastructure/Consumers and apps/bmf into the skills, which teaches a Python or TS agent that the tool thinks in PHP. shanpan is polyglot; its guidance must read that way

cl: The PHP parser resolves calls on $this->prop by building a per-file class→(property→declared type) map from typed property declarations and constructor-promoted parameters, then emitting Type.method as the call target; unions/intersections are left unresolved rather than guessed
bc: injected-dependency calls ($this->l1Cache->clearMemory()) are the dominant Symfony/PHP call pattern and were dropped for want of type inference, so the call graph missed the edges agents needed and grep won. The map is file-local because a property read and its call share a class in the same file

cl: Call resolution walks the caller class's ancestors (extends + used traits) via a per-run inheritance map before the name-suffix fallback, so $this->method() resolves to the defining parent class precisely instead of matching an arbitrary same-named method. EXTENDS edges are stored (child→parent CodeSymbol) for override queries and to rebuild the map on incremental analyze
bc: the old suffix match resolved .clear to any X.clear, giving wrong or empty call edges; agents needed 'who clears?' answered. Inheritance data is name-based (PHP class names are effectively global), parents without a graph symbol stay in the map but get no edge

cl: analyze must call ensureSchema before writing — it can create tables (e.g. EXTENDS) that a pre-upgrade graph lacks. Previously only init, records index, and MCP startup ran ensureSchema, so analyze on an older graph would fail the moment it tried to write a newly-added edge type
